description: Found in examples/hll_update_many.exs (defk-9p6.15). Defk.Bench.best/2 calls :erlang.garbage_collect() before each timed run; a full sweep puts the live data, including a 100k-element list of u64s (half bignums, ~500k words) the timed fun reads, into the new young heap rather than the old generation. The next minor GC inside the timed run copies the whole list (~0.6 ms here). A side that allocates little (defk: pack the list + kernel, 0.36 ms) pays it in some runs only, so best-of-7 gives 0.36-0.38 ms but the sweep's best-of-3 gave 1.06 ms in 4 of 4 runs; the Elixir side allocates enough to pay it every run. Measured with :erlang.statistics(:garbage_collection): packing 100k hashes takes ~270-460 us with 0 GCs and ~850-1100 us with 1 GC that reclaims 163 words (i.e. a copy of live data, not garbage). Options: a second garbage_collect (or a minor GC) after the full one so the inputs are promoted to the old heap, or run each timed call in a fresh process given a copy of the inputs, or document it. Either way both sides are treated alike; the question is which state is realistic (a freshly built list is young too).

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Defk.Bench promotes the caller's live inputs to the old heap before timing, so a minor GC copying them does not land in some timed runs

**Decision (maintainer, triage 2026-10-11):** a second garbage collection after the full one, so inputs sit in the old generation like long-lived data a real caller holds; both sides treated alike; documented.

**Current behavior:**
`Defk.Bench` runs `:erlang.garbage_collect()` before each timed run. The full sweep leaves the live data (e.g. a 100k-element u64 list in examples/hll_update_many.exs) in the new young heap, and the next minor GC inside the timed run copies it (~0.6 ms there). A side that allocates little pays it only in some runs (best-of-3 1.06 ms vs best-of-7 0.36 ms).

**Desired behavior:**
- Before each timed run, the benchmark process's live data is in the old heap (verify with `:erlang.process_info(self(), [:heap_size, :total_heap_size])`/`:garbage_collection` stats or by the absence of a minor GC copying live data during the timed run), for both the defk and Elixir sides.
- The Defk.Bench docs state the heap state the timing starts from and why.
- If two collections do not reliably promote (e.g. depends on fullsweep_after or min_heap_size), use the smallest reliable mechanism and explain it in the report.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A test (bench_test) shows that after the bench's pre-run collection a large input list no longer triggers a minor GC that copies it during a low-allocation timed function (e.g. :erlang.statistics(:garbage_collection) words reclaimed / number of GCs)
- [ ] examples/hll_update_many.exs: the sweep's best-of-3 and best-of-7 agree within noise; record before/after numbers in docs/performance.md (mark provisional if loaded)
- [ ] `mix test`, `mix docs`, `mix credo --strict` clean

**Out of scope:**
- Running timed calls in a fresh process; changing best-of counts

title: Defk.Bench forced full GC leaves the caller's input list in the young heap: a minor GC copying it lands in some timed runs
